# ssh-cli


> One-shot multi-host SSH command-line interface (CLI) for AI agents with X Desktop Group (XDG) storage and no Node daemon

ssh-cli is a memory-safe Rust binary that lets large language model (LLM) agents operate remote servers over SSH through stdin and stdout. Each call is born, runs one operation and dies: it keeps no daemon, sends no telemetry, stores a multi-host registry under XDG with secrets encrypted at rest, and exposes 48 leaf commands with 25 JSON schemas in version 0.5.6.

- Read this document in [Portuguese (pt-BR)](https://github.com/danilo-aguiar-br/ssh-cli/blob/main/llms.pt-BR.txt)
- Expanded index with every flag and schema: [llms-full.txt](https://github.com/danilo-aguiar-br/ssh-cli/blob/main/llms-full.txt)

## Quick start
- `cargo install ssh-cli --locked`: installs ssh-cli 0.5.6, which needs Rust 1.89 or newer
- `printf '%s' "$PASS" | ssh-cli vps add --name prod --host h.example --user deploy --password-stdin --json`: registers a host once without a password on argv
- `ssh-cli exec prod 'hostname' --json`: runs one remote command and prints one JSON object
- `ssh-cli doctor --json`: preflight for paths, encryption at rest and the config directory mode
- `ssh-cli commands --json`: full command tree with every argument of every command
- `ssh-cli schema`: catalog of the 25 embedded JSON schemas, and `ssh-cli schema <NAME>` prints one


## Agent rules
### Authentication
- Pass secrets with `--password-stdin`, `--key`, `--key-passphrase-stdin` or `--use-agent`, never as an argv value
- `vps edit --key`, `--password` or `--password-stdin`, and `--use-agent` switch the stored method in one call and clear the opposite fields
- `updated` in the `vps-edited` event names the new method and only the cleared fields that held a value
- Two primary auth flags in one call exit 2, and a passphrase without any key exits 64 and leaves the record untouched
- A different `--key` path drops the old passphrase unless the call brings a new one, and `--agent-socket` alone implies `--use-agent`
- `--no-key` exits 64 when the key was the only authentication, and `--no-agent-socket` exits 64 on Unix when it would leave the agent without an endpoint
- After an auth rejection (exit 77) try another method, and review a TOFU host-key error before using `--replace-host-key`

### Host names
- `vps add`, `vps rename`, `vps edit --name` and `vps import` accept only 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore, starting with a letter or digit
- Any other name exits 64, and a name such as `bad name`, `x;y` or one with an ESC byte never reaches the registry
- `vps import` checks every item first, lists all invalid names at once, writes nothing and gives the same error under `--dry-run`
- Names already stored with a space or an accent still load, list, show and resolve
- A stored name with control or bidi characters loads too, `doctor` lists it escaped in `local.invalid_host_names`, and `vps rename '<legacy name>' <new>` repairs it
- Lookups that become a target (`exec`, `health-check`, `--hosts` and `connect`) refuse control and bidi characters with exit 64, and `connect` writes no marker
- `tls mtls import --name` refuses control, formatting and bidi characters with exit 64 and creates no directory, while `serviço-1` stays valid
- `vps rename` exits 64 with `vps_duplicate` when the destination exists, and exits 64 when the new name equals the current one
- The registry is keyed by the NFC record name, and two tables that normalize to the same name exit 65 with `config has two hosts named ...`

### Terminal safety
- Text mode writes control, formatting and bidi characters as escapes such as `\u{1b}` in messages, errors, `list`, `show`, `health-check`, `doctor` and batch output
- `sftp ls` and `sftp stat` also escape `\n` and `\t` inside remote names, so a hostile name cannot forge extra lines
- JSON output keeps the stored value unchanged because it is for machines
- The remote stdout and stderr of `exec` stay raw by design, so never print them to a terminal without your own filter

### Doctor and config directory
- `ssh-cli doctor --json` reports `local.config_dir_permissions`, `local.config_dir_exposed`, `local.invalid_host_names` and `local.active_vps`
- `--select` and `--truncate-content` reduce a single record, while `--filter`, `--limit`, `--sort`, `--dedupe-by`, `--count-only` and `--max-output-bytes` stay inert there and are named under `agent_shape.ignored`
- Read one field with `ssh-cli doctor --json --select local.config_dir_exposed`
- A config directory level created by the CLI gets mode 0700, and `config.toml`, `known_hosts.lock` and `lang` are created 0600
- An existing directory is tightened to 0700 only when it is the default XDG directory, not a symlink and owned by the current user
- Any other existing directory keeps its mode, so `config_dir_exposed: true` means the operator must run `chmod 700` on it
- `--config-dir <path>.toml` makes the parent the config directory for the registry, `secrets.key`, `known_hosts`, `active`, `lang` and the TLS files
- `vps export -o new/deep/e.json` creates the missing directories 0700 and never changes an existing one

### Preview with dry-run
- `--dry-run` is accepted only by `vps remove`, `vps import`, `vps edit`, `vps rename`, `sftp rm`, `sftp rmdir`, `secrets init` and `secrets reencrypt`
- Anywhere else `--dry-run` exits 64 instead of being accepted and ignored
- The plan is a `dry-run` event with `operation`, `executed: false`, `target_resolved`, `target_source` (`argv`), `host_resolved` and `host_source`, as in `docs/schemas/dry-run.schema.json`
- `vps edit`, `vps rename` and `vps remove`, real or dry, exit 66 on a missing registry or host and create no directory and no lock file
- Both previews of `vps edit` and `vps rename` run every validation of the real run and stop before the write

### Targets
- Always name the target: `exec <VPS> <COMMAND>`, or a selector (`--all`, `--hosts` or `--tags`) with one positional
- A lone positional on `exec`, `sudo-exec` or `su-exec` exits 64, because the host name would otherwise run as a remote binary
- `connect <NAME>` writes the active marker, and only `--use-active` with `<COMMAND>` reaches it, with exit 66 when no marker exists
- Read the target back from `target_resolved` and `target_source` (`argv`, `active_marker` or `selector`) and from `active_fallback`
- `host_resolved` and `host_source` are the 0.5.5 read aliases of the two canonical fields

### Output and errors
- Success JSON goes to stdout, and with `--json` or a non-TTY stdout a failure writes its envelope to stderr
- A failure before any remote work leaves stdout empty, while a remote command that ran and failed keeps its `exec` JSON on stdout
- A failed remote command exits 1: the `exec` JSON on stdout has the remote `exit_code`, and the stderr envelope `command_failed` carries `remote_exit_code`
- A partial fleet failure prints the batch JSON on stdout plus a `partial_failure` envelope on stderr, also with exit 1
- Usage errors are plain text on stderr with no JSON envelope: the exit 2 of the argument parser and the exit 64 of a malformed `--filter`
- Only runtime errors carry the JSON envelope, so parse the stderr of a non-zero exit as JSON only after the exit code is neither 2 nor a usage 64
- The failure envelope has `exit_code`, `error_code`, `message`, `error_class`, `retryable` and `suggestion`, as in `docs/schemas/error-envelope.schema.json`
- Read the exit code first, then the stream that matches it, and never parse tracing lines on stderr
- Retry only when `retryable` is true, which covers IO, timeouts and the busy config lock, and never retry auth, usage or data errors
- Error bodies stay in English by design, so the agent receives stable text
- Default tracing is `error`, ambient `RUST_LOG` is ignored, and `-v`, `-vv` and `-vvv` raise it, always scoped to this crate

### Payload shaping
- `--select` (alias `--fields`), `--filter`, `--limit`, `--sort`, `--dedupe-by`, `--count-only`, `--truncate-content` and `--max-output-bytes` are global and run before serialization
- The collection flags reduce the top-level array of `vps list`, the `results` array of batch envelopes and the `entries` array of `sftp ls`
- A single object such as `exec` on one host, `vps show` and `doctor` is reduced by `--select` and `--truncate-content`, so `ssh-cli doctor --json --select local.config_dir_exposed` returns one field
- The collection flags `--filter`, `--limit`, `--sort`, `--dedupe-by`, `--count-only` and `--max-output-bytes` cannot apply to one record, so they are named in `agent_shape.ignored`
- `--select` names the fields of each record, so on a batch envelope use `--select name,stdout` and not `--select results`
- A shaped envelope gains `agent_shape` with `input_count`, `output_count` and `dropped`, and a shaped single object gains `selected`, `content_truncated` and `ignored`
- A reduced bare array such as `vps list` has no room for `agent_shape`, so its report reaches stderr as one JSON line with `"event":"agent-shape"` and `--quiet` suppresses it
- `--filter` takes `key=value`, `key!=value` or `key~substring`, repeatable with AND, and a malformed predicate is rejected at parse time
- `--no-input` refuses to read stdin, so combine it with a flag value instead of `--password-stdin`

### Import and export
- `vps export` prints JSON on any non-TTY stdout, even into a `.toml` filename, and TOML only with `--output-format text`
- A redacted export has empty secrets and never an `sshcli-enc:` blob of empty, so importing it needs `--allow-incomplete`
- `--include-secrets` into a pipe needs `-o <PATH>` or `--i-understand-secrets-on-stdout`, and it exits 64 otherwise
- `vps import --file <PATH>` accepts TOML with EN keys such as `username` plus legacy PT keys, or a JSON `vps-export` envelope, and bad TOML exits 65
- The `vps-import` event carries `imported` and the sorted, always present `replaced` list
- Never use export, edit and import to rename a host, because `vps rename` keeps every credential and the detour dropped agent authentication
- A legacy host whose name fails the strict charset exports fine but restores only after `vps rename` gives it a strict name

### Fleet
- Prefer one process with `--all`, `--hosts a,b` or `--tags` over N single-host spawns
- `--tags` exists on `exec`, `sudo-exec` and `su-exec`, while `scp`, `sftp` and `health-check` take `--all` and `--hosts`
- Batch envelopes (`exec-batch`, `scp-batch`, `sftp-batch`, `health-check-batch`) carry `max_concurrency`, and on cancel the remainder is filled as cancelled so `results.len() == input.len()`
- `health-check --all` returns `results[].status` (`ok` or `error`) plus `error`, so list the failures with `--filter status!=ok`, while `exec-batch` results carry `ok`
- Partial multi-host failure exits 1, and `--fail-fast` stops admitting new units after the first failure
- `vps doctor --probe-ssh [--hosts a,b] --json` emits one `vps-doctor` document with `local` and `ssh_probe`

### Transfers and tunnels
- `scp upload|download` moves regular files only, with no `-r`, and `--json` emits `scp-transfer` as in `docs/schemas/scp-transfer.schema.json`
- mtime and mode preservation is best effort, so read `mtime_preserved` and `durable` for the real outcome
- A missing remote file exits 66 with `file not found: <path>`, and a download writes `.ssh-cli.partial`, runs `sync_data` and then renames
- Prefer 0.5.3 or newer for SFTP, where upload never truncates to 0 bytes and the SETSTAT call sends atime and mtime together
- SFTP upload masks modes with `SFTP_PERM_MASK` (0o7777) and download with `SFTP_PERM_MASK_UNTRUSTED` (0o0777), so server-sent setuid, setgid and sticky bits never reach a local file
- `tunnel` always needs `--timeout-ms`, and a deadline after the bind exits 0 while a timeout before the bind exits 74
- `tunnel` stopped by SIGINT exits 130 and by SIGTERM exits 143, and `tunnel_closed` carries `reason: signal`
- `tunnel` has four exclusive modes: the default local forward, `--socks5`, `--remote-socket <PATH>` and `--reverse`
- The JSON `mode` is `local`, `reverse`, `socks5` or `streamlocal`, and `tunnel_listening` and `tunnel_closed` both carry it
- A non-loopback `--bind` requires `--i-accept-network-exposure`, and under `--reverse` that flag guards the bind of the server
- Wait for `tunnel_listening` before using the local port, and read `tunnel_closed` (`reason`, `forwards_served`, `capacity_waits`) to learn why it ended

### Secrets and configuration
- Secrets in `config.toml` are encrypted by default with ChaCha20-Poly1305 and an auto-created `secrets.key`, and the first secret write reports `secrets_key_auto_created: true` in the same `vps-added` document
- Configure the product with CLI flags (`--allow-plaintext-secrets`, `--secrets-key-file`, `--use-keyring`) and XDG files, never with environment variables
- `SSH_CLI_SECRETS_*` variables fail closed when present, and there is no `.env` product store
- Never print or log host passwords, the master key or decrypted secrets, and `-vvv` does not dump russh password traffic
- `tls acme issue`, `tls acme complete` and `tls acme status` take the domain as `--domain <DOMAIN>`, and a positional domain exits 2
- A redacted `vps export` writes `password` as an empty string and the other secrets as `null`, while the three-asterisk mask appears only in `vps list` and `vps show`
- The config lock waits `--lock-wait-ms` (default 5000, maximum 300000) and then exits 69 instead of hanging
- Telemetry is always false, and the product never runs a daemon


## Command reference
- `ssh-cli vps add`: Adds a new VPS to the registry
- `ssh-cli vps list`: Lists all VPS hosts (passwords masked)
- `ssh-cli vps remove`: Removes a VPS from the registry
- `ssh-cli vps rename`: Renames a registered VPS without touching credentials
- `ssh-cli vps edit`: Edits fields of an existing VPS
- `ssh-cli vps show`: Shows VPS details (passwords masked)
- `ssh-cli vps path`: Shows the configuration file path
- `ssh-cli vps doctor`: Diagnostics for XDG layers / path / schema
- `ssh-cli vps export`: Exports hosts (passwords redacted by default)
- `ssh-cli vps import`: Imports hosts from a TOML file or JSON `vps-export` envelope (EN + legacy PT keys)
- `ssh-cli connect`: Sets the active VPS (writes sibling `active` file in the config directory)
- `ssh-cli exec`: Runs a command on the VPS over SSH (stdout/stderr captured)
- `ssh-cli sudo-exec`: Runs a command with `sudo` (safe `sh -c` packing)
- `ssh-cli su-exec`: Runs a command with one-shot `su -` elevation
- `ssh-cli scp upload`: Uploads a local file to the remote host (regular files only)
- `ssh-cli scp download`: Downloads a remote file to the local host (regular files only)
- `ssh-cli sftp upload`: Uploads a local file or tree to the remote host via SFTP
- `ssh-cli sftp download`: Downloads a remote file or tree to the local host via SFTP
- `ssh-cli sftp ls`: Lists a remote directory
- `ssh-cli sftp mkdir`: Creates a remote directory
- `ssh-cli sftp rmdir`: Removes an empty remote directory
- `ssh-cli sftp rm`: Removes a remote file
- `ssh-cli sftp stat`: Shows metadata for a remote path
- `ssh-cli sftp rename`: Renames a remote path
- `ssh-cli tunnel`: SSH tunnel with mandatory deadline (bounded one-shot)
- `ssh-cli health-check`: Checks SSH connectivity to a VPS (`--all` / `--hosts` / `--use-active`)
- `ssh-cli secrets status`: Shows encryption status (no sensitive material)
- `ssh-cli secrets init`: Generates and stores the primary key (`secrets.key` or keyring) and never prints the key
- `ssh-cli secrets reencrypt`: Rewrites `config.toml` re-encrypting secrets with the current key
- `ssh-cli completions`: Generates shell completions
- `ssh-cli commands`: Emits the full command tree as JSON (agent discovery / rules `mycli commands`)
- `ssh-cli schema`: Emits embedded JSON Schema catalog or one schema body (G-E2E-02)
- `ssh-cli doctor`: Root alias for `vps doctor` (XDG / schema diagnostics, G-E2E-03)
- `ssh-cli locale show`: Shows resolved language, winning layer, and available locales (default)
- `ssh-cli locale set`: Persists preferred language under the config directory (`lang` file, 0o600)
- `ssh-cli locale clear`: Removes the persisted language preference
- `ssh-cli tls provider`: Shows rustls CryptoProvider status (`aws_lc_rs`)
- `ssh-cli tls paths`: Prints XDG TLS directory layout paths
- `ssh-cli tls mtls list`: Lists imported identity names
- `ssh-cli tls mtls import`: Imports PEM cert+key as a named identity
- `ssh-cli tls mtls show`: Shows paths for one identity
- `ssh-cli tls mtls remove`: Removes an identity directory
- `ssh-cli tls acme account create`: Creates an ACME account (credentials under XDG `tls/acme/account.json`, 0o600)
- `ssh-cli tls acme account show`: Shows whether an account exists and its path
- `ssh-cli tls acme issue`: Starts DNS-01 order and prints the TXT challenge (persists order URL under XDG)
- `ssh-cli tls acme complete`: Completes a pending order after DNS TXT is published
- `ssh-cli tls acme status`: Shows certificate / pending status for one domain or all
- `ssh-cli tls acme list`: Lists ACME domain directories under XDG


## Global flags
- `--lang <LOCALE>`: Forces the CLI language (`en` or `pt-BR`, and BCP47 tags negotiate to them)
- `-v, --verbose`: Raises log verbosity on stderr (`-v` info, `-vv` debug, `-vvv` trace), always scoped to this crate
- `-q, --quiet`: Suppresses non-JSON output
- `--config-dir <DIR>`: Overrides the configuration directory, and a path ending in `.toml` makes its parent the directory
- `--no-color`: Disables colored output
- `--output-format <text|json>`: Chooses `text` or `json`, and JSON is the default when stdout is not a TTY
- `--json`: Forces JSON output, alias of `--output-format json`
- `--select <PATHS>`: Keeps only these dotted paths in each record (CSV, alias `--fields`)
- `--filter <EXPR>`: Keeps records matching `key=value`, `key!=value` or `key~substring`, repeatable with AND
- `--limit <N>`: Emits at most N records
- `--sort <PATH>`: Sorts records ascending by dotted path, comparing numbers numerically
- `--dedupe-by <PATH>`: Drops later records that repeat the value of this dotted path
- `--count-only`: Replaces the record collection with `{"count": N}`, counted after filtering
- `--truncate-content <CHARS>`: Shortens strings longer than N characters, never bytes
- `--max-output-bytes <BYTES>`: Caps the envelope size by dropping trailing records, never by slicing the JSON text
- `--no-input`: Refuses to read stdin and fails fast instead of blocking
- `--dry-run`: Prints the plan and exits without executing, accepted only by eight operations and rejected with exit 64 elsewhere
- `--lock-wait-ms <MS>`: Bounds the wait for the config lock (default 5000, maximum 300000) before exit 69
- `--disable-sudo`: Disables `sudo-exec` and `su-exec` for this invocation (alias `--disableSudo`), and placed before `vps add` or `vps edit` it also writes `disable_sudo` to the host
- `--replace-host-key`: Replaces a diverging host key in the TOFU `known_hosts`
- `--allow-plaintext-secrets`: Allows plaintext secrets at rest, for tests only
- `--secrets-key-file <PATH>`: Reads the 64-hex primary key from this file for one invocation
- `--use-keyring`: Prefers the OS keyring for the primary key
- `--timeout <MS>`: Sets the global SSH timeout in milliseconds, and a local `--timeout` wins while `tunnel` still needs `--timeout-ms`
- `--max-concurrency <N>`: Caps concurrent multi-host sessions and tunnel forwards, from 1 to 64
- `--fail-fast`: Stops admitting new multi-host units after the first failure
- `--scp-file-concurrency <N>`: Sets concurrent SCP transfers on one SSH session (default 1)


## Exit codes
- `0`: success
- `1`: runtime failure, remote command failure or partial multi-host failure
- `2`: clap usage error, such as conflicting flags or an invalid value
- `64`: usage error detected by the product
- `65`: data error in TOML, JSON, config or schema
- `66`: VPS, active marker or file not found
- `69`: service unavailable, such as the config lock still busy after `--lock-wait-ms` or a locked keyring
- `70`: internal software error
- `73`: cannot create config output
- `74`: IO error, SSH connection error or timeout
- `77`: authentication rejected, host key changed or sudo policy refused
- `130`: SIGINT
- `141`: broken pipe on stdout or stderr
- `143`: SIGTERM
- `ssh-cli --help` ends with an `Exit status:` section that lists these 14 codes
- All 48 leaf commands carry an `Examples:` block in their `--help`, and `tests/docs_conformance.rs` runs every published argv with `--help` appended to prove it parses


## Release notes
- 0.5.6 reduces a single record with `--select` and `--truncate-content`, reports a bare-array reduction on stderr as `{"event":"agent-shape",...}`, names ignored collection flags under `agent_shape.ignored`, and shows an `Examples:` block on all 48 leaves
- 0.5.6 adds `vps rename <NAME> <NEW_NAME>` and `vps edit <NAME> --name <NEW>`, which rename natively and keep every credential readable under the new name
- 0.5.6 adds eight clear flags to `vps edit`: `--clear-tags`, `--clear-sudo-password`, `--clear-su-password`, `--no-tls-sni`, `--no-tls-client-cert`, `--no-tls-client-key`, `--no-key` and `--no-agent-socket`
- 0.5.6 extends `--dry-run` to `vps edit` and `vps rename`, bounds the config lock with `--lock-wait-ms` into exit 69, and makes `commands --json` publish every argument
- 0.5.6 closes the gaps found by the end-to-end audit and the independent reviews: strict host names, escaped terminal output, private config directories, auth switching and a clean package
- 0.5.6 is BREAKING for scripts, because `vps edit` now switches the auth method where it used to exit 64, and the release scripts became Python programs
- 0.5.6 is BREAKING for library users: the `Money` module and the `rust_decimal` dependency are gone and `SshCliError::Unavailable` carries `UnavailableService`
- 0.5.5 fixes GAP-SSH-EXEC-ARGC-001, where the exec family chose the target host by positional count, and it is BREAKING because a lone positional is now a usage error
- 0.5.5 adds `--use-active` with `<COMMAND>` plus `target_resolved`, `target_source` and `active_fallback` on every envelope, and `doctor` reports `local.active_vps`
- 0.5.4 fixes a remote pre-auth DoS in the SSH banner path (A1), stops server-sent setuid bits on downloads (A3) and closes the world-readable window on ACME and mTLS private keys (A2)
- 0.5.4 adds `tunnel --reverse`, `tunnel --socks5`, `tunnel --remote-socket`, the `tunnel_closed` event and the eight payload-shaping flags
- 0.5.4 is BREAKING because partial multi-host failure exits 1 (it was 65) and a non-loopback `--bind` requires `--i-accept-network-exposure`
